rows.title: Sr Product Manager - Enterprise Risk
rows.descriptionText:
Senior Product Manager, Enterprise & Payment Risk

About The Role

Uber's Risk team is critical to enabling trusted growth across our global marketplace by preventing fraud and abuse while minimizing friction for legitimate users. Enterprise (B2B) accounts are a major and fast-growing part of that marketplace, and managing their risk is one of the most structurally complex domains in Payment Risk.

In this senior, high-impact individual contributor role, the Product Manager for Enterprise & Payment Risk will own the full risk lifecycle of B2B entities at scale - from onboarding and information acquisition, through manual review processes, to real-time risk decisioning at checkout and payment. The role also owns the underlying account and billing infrastructure that enterprise risk decisions run on, and the recovery/verification experiences enterprise customers rely on when something goes wrong.

A defining challenge of this role is that the enterprise customer base spans many distinct cohorts, each with a different risk tolerance and a different sensitivity to friction and actioning. Success requires calibrating risk treatment differently across these cohorts rather than applying a single, one-size-fits-all policy - balancing fraud prevention against growth and satisfaction for legitimate business customers. This is the most stakeholder-intensive scope in the Payment Risk organization, requiring close, sustained partnership with business/BD leadership in addition to Engineering, Data Science, and platform teams.

This position is ideal for a senior product leader who thrives in ambiguous, high-stakes problem spaces, has strong command of B2B/enterprise payment or billing systems, and can drive outcomes through influence across a large and often-competing set of stakeholders and shared engineering capacity.

What The Candidate Will Do

Own the B2B entity risk lifecycle end-to-end at scale: onboarding and information acquisition, manual review workflows, and real-time risk decisioning at checkout and payment. Segment and calibrate risk policy across distinct enterprise customer cohorts, each with different risk tolerance and sensitivity to friction/actioning. Define the product requirements and roadmap for enterprise risk capabilities, including underlying account and billing infrastructure modernization and its associated cross-functional dependencies. Own recovery and verification experiences for enterprise customers, including fallback challenges, admin verification, and cross-party messaging. Partner with Engineering and Data Science to scope and land payment authorization and decisioning improvements against concrete loss-reduction targets. Triage, prioritize, and negotiate a high volume of cross-functional dependency requests against shared and constrained engineering capacity. Build and maintain trusted relationships with business/BD stakeholders, translating enterprise account needs into a risk product roadmap. Measure impact using well-defined KPIs (e.g., loss-rate reduction, authorization effectiveness, dispute/chargeback rates) and iterate based on learnings. Coordinate with Risk Operations, Risk Governance/Compliance, and payments platform teams to ensure solutions are practical, compliant, and operationally sound. 

Basic Qualifications

8+ years of product management experience delivering software products as an individual contributor in a technology company. Experience owning a complex, technically deep product domain (e.g., payments, billing, risk, or platform infrastructure) with significant stakeholder breadth. Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to inform decisions and measure impact. Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex problems simply to both technical and business audiences. Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Engineering, Data Science, Business/BD, Design, and Operations, including negotiating priority against shared/constrained resources. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data/Analytics, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent experience). 

Preferred Qualifications

Risk & Fraud Domain Expertise - Experience in risk, fraud, or trust & safety within a B2B/enterprise or multi-sided marketplace, particularly billing risk, checkout/payment decisioning, or auth-hold systems. B2B/Enterprise Product Ownership - Prior ownership of a product serving business or organizational accounts (rather than purely consumer-facing products), including billing configuration, credit management, or account administration. Business Acumen - Demonstrated ability to drive P&L improvements through loss reduction or account-health initiatives, with strong intuition for how risk interventions affect the broader business. Strategic Judgment - Strong product instincts for navigating ambiguous, structurally complex problem spaces and balancing competing constraints across risk, business, engineering capacity, and compliance. Advanced Business Education - MBA or equivalent business experience. 

Extra notes:

Prefer candidates with prior experience in engineering, data scientist, consulting, finance, or a B2B/enterprise SaaS product role before moving into PM, given the domain's billing/payments complexity.

rows.title: 2027 Internal Audit Analyst Summer Internship Program Whippany
rows.descriptionText:
Explore the world of Barclays as a Summer Intern

Spend 10 weeks diving into real projects, gaining hands-on experience, and shaping your future. You’ll receive full support, take on meaningful responsibilities, and build lasting connections—all while discovering what makes our culture unique.

If you're in your penultimate year and ready to grow, learn, and make an impact, this is your opportunity to belong and thrive.

Why the Internal Audit Internship program? 

Barclays Internal Audit (BIA) plays a key role in our business worldwide. Independent assurance and insightful challenge are at the heart of what we do, helping to protect Barclays' assets, reputation, and sustainability, while supporting the management of current and emerging risks in an increasingly digital, technology-driven world.

We're an independent control function that provides objective, reliable, and insightful assurance to the Board and Executive Management. Known as the "third line of defence", we work closely with the business to help strengthen governance, risk management, and controls. We do this by regularly reviewing and assessing business areas across the bank, evaluating how effectively risks are managed and whether controls are operating as intended. We then report our findings and work with stakeholders to help drive meaningful improvements and ensure issues are resolved effectively.

Barclays Internal Audit is a leader in Data Analytics and other specialist areas, using innovative approaches and technology to enhance the way we provide assurance. We've built a strong reputation in the financial services industry for our expertise, fresh thinking, and forward-looking approach.

This is your chance to work in an area that has a real impact across the bank, gain unique insight into how Barclays operates, and work alongside experts who will help you build the skills, knowledge, and experience needed for a successful career.

To be eligible for this opportunity, you must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 and have a GPA of 3.2 or above. While a STEM degree (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) can be a great fit for the analytical nature of Internal Audit, it’s not essential. We value diverse perspectives and encourage students from any field of study to apply.

Ideally, you’ll also be naturally analytical, eager to learn, and ready to take on new challenges. You know how to manage your time, build strong relationships, and thrive in a team.

The location for this role is indicated in the job title, and you will be based at that location. If you are successful in receiving a return offer to our graduate program, your location will be the same as it was during your internship.

Barclays will not offer or consider offering sponsorship for work visas or offer any employment-based immigration sponsorship for individuals, now or in the future, unless such individuals are enrolled in or graduate with a degree in a field of study that the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Education consider to be a science, technology, engineering or mathematics (STEM) field of study for purposes of the 24-month STEM OPT extension. This includes for any internship, post-graduation program, or permanent employment, now or in the future.

Working in Whippany

Our next-gen workplace in Whippany is where passionate, down-to-earth colleagues connect daily. With modern workspaces, cafés, pool tables, and a gym, it’s a place that feels like home.

Off campus, you’re minutes from historic Morristown and just a short trip to the buzz of Manhattan—Whippany offers the best of both worlds.

Salary / Rate Minimum: $78,000

Purpose of the role

About The Role And Team

As a Staff Scientist at Uber, you will solve the complex, global-scale puzzle of how millions of people and things move in the real world. Operating as a technical multiplier at the high-stakes intersection of digital systems and physical movement, you will navigate extreme ambiguity, set scientific strategy, and make critical decisions with imperfect information. Whether you are architecting next-generation marketplace mechanisms or defining experimentation guardrails, you will thrive in an environment where high performance and massive scale are inextricably linked.

You will join the Rider Pricing and Incentive team, which owns the real-time algorithms powering our mobility business. In this role, you will define the scientific strategy for measuring marketplace performance and optimizing complex pricing systems. Beyond building models, you will develop data insights to identify high-impact opportunities and influence executive roadmaps. You will also drive execution by providing technical guidance to junior scientists and partnering cross-functionally with Product and Engineering teams to deliver high-impact, productionized results.

What You'll Do

 Set Scientific Vision: Define the 1-2 year scientific strategy and technical roadmap for real-time rider pricing, identifying high-impact opportunities.  Lead the Architecture and Design: Define the scientific frameworks and next-generation pricing algorithms that ensure our models are modular, extensible, and observable at global scale.  Act as a Technical Multiplier: Elevate team-wide technical execution by identifying opportunities for system efficiency, model performance, and reduction of technical debt across software and science pipelines.  Influence Senior Leadership: Partner directly with Product, Engineering, and Business Executives, translating complex data and technical findings into clear strategic recommendations.  Own Technical Trajectory: Direct the evolution of critical pricing systems, balancing short-term needs with long-term scalability and efficiency.  Establish Scientific Guardrails: Set experimentation standards and statistical frameworks across multiple teams, driving organization-wide adoption of best practices in causal inference and marketplace testing. 

Basic Qualifications

 Ph.D., M.S., or B.S. in Economics, Operations Research, Statistics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or related quantitative fields.  Minimum of 6+ years (M.S./Ph.D.) or 8+ years (B.S.) of industry experience building, deploying, and scaling quantitative models in production environments.  Deep expertise in statistical inference, advanced experimental design (e.g., switchbacks, cluster-randomized trials), and quantitative economic modeling.  Proficiency in SQL and Python working with large-scale distributed data tools (e.g., Spark, Presto). 

Preferred Qualifications

 Domain Mastery: Recognized expertise in marketplace design, pricing algorithms, industrial organization, ML system design, or large-scale optimization in high-throughput environments. rows.descriptionText:
Embark on a transformative journey as a Senior Product Owner. At Barclays, our vision is clear –to redefine the future of banking and help craft innovative solutions. In this role, you will shape the future of customer engagement through innovative marketing technology solutions. In this high-impact position, you will drive the strategy and delivery of industry-leading MarTech capabilities that enable personalized, data-driven experiences, helping Barclays deepen customer relationships and support its long-term growth goals. You'll have the unique opportunity to influence enterprise-scale platforms, collaborate with senior stakeholders across the organization, and drive strategic customer experience outcomes through market-leading MarTech platforms across the Adobe Experience Cloud ecosystem and beyond.

To be successful as a Senior Product Owner, you should:


Drive and oversee the product vision, roadmap, and backlog, ensuring alignment with marketing, customer communication, and enterprise targetsExcel at prioritization and sound judgment by balancing business value, customer experience, risk, compliance, and technical feasibilityTranslate business and marketing requirements into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and actionable outcomes for Agile delivery teamsBuild considerable relationships across business and technology teams to drive stakeholder alignment, collaboration, and executionApply Agile and data-driven practices to continuously improve customer experiences, platform adoption, operational efficiency, and product performance

Deep knowledge across Adobe Experience Cloud, Adobe Campaign, AEM, Tealium, Transactional Databases, CMS, customer communication, personalization, and analytics platformsConsiderable technical acumen with APIs, integrations, cloud technologies, data flows, and enterprise platform architecturesExperience in banking or financial services, with knowledge of security, compliance, data privacy, governance, and large-scale digital transformation programs


You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for success in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking, digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.

This role is located in our Whippany, NJ office.

Maximum Salary: $230,000

The minimum and maximum salary/rate information above include only base salary or base hourly rate. It does not include any other type of compensation or benefits that may be available.

Barclays employees are eligible for a suite of competitive and generous employee benefits, including medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k), life insurance, and other paid leave for qualifying circumstances.

This position is eligible for an incentive award.

Purpose

The purpose of a Product Owner is to maximize the value of the product by defining a clear product vision (are they setting the vision or would this align to ), managing authoring, refining and prioritizing the Product Backlog balancing trade-offs across desirability, viability and feasibility – making sure the right thing is being ‘built’, and prioritising work based on business goals. They act as the primary liaison between stakeholders and delivery teams, ensuring the product meets user/customer needs and delivers optimal value. Product Owners are responsible for developing a roadmap and driving execution of their product area/sub-journey, applying continuous improvement principles and techniques.

Accountabilities


Ensure Product Alignment with Business Goals: Ensure that the product & its features are aligned with broader objectives, driving value and contributing to the organization’s overall strategy. Utilisation of market research, analysis of customer feedback and monitoring of industry trends to identify new products, features or enhancements.  Communicate Product Vision to Delivery Teams: Clearly articulate the product vision and goals to the delivery teams, ensuring they understand, align and are inspired to deliver the business value and purpose of each feature or user story.Create and Refine User Stories: Write clear, concise user stories with detailed acceptance criteria, refining them as needed to ensure the development team has all the necessary information to implement features successfully. Managing the Product Backlog: Responsible for creating, maintaining, and prioritising the product backlog, ensuring the highest value features are delivered first, based on business needs, customer requirements and organisational impacts, balancing risk migration and future proofing against the product strategy. Manage on-going readiness and 'run' activities of live products including monitoring, governance and approvals. rows.descriptionText:
About Team

At Uber, we're not just moving people and things; we're building a global business grounded in integrity. Our Financial Risk Management (FRM) Advisory team is the backbone of that integrity, ensuring our financial reporting is accurate, trustworthy, and compliant with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX).

As a Senior on this team, you'll be on the front lines, safeguarding our financial data and helping us navigate the complexities of a dynamic, global company. This isn't just about checking boxes-it's about asking the right questions, acting with conviction, and boldly improving our processes to drive meaningful outcomes and maintain the trust of our stakeholders.

What You Will Do

Uber's technology platform reimagines the way people and things move in cities around the world by connecting drivers, riders, and eaters. We offer a variety of services including:

Ridesharing: Connecting riders with drivers for convenient transportation. Delivery: Connecting consumers with restaurants and stores for food, groceries, and other deliveries. Freight: Connecting shippers and carriers in the logistics space. 

Job Responsibilities - FRM Advisory Senior - Business Process

Strategic Risk Advisory & Governance: Serve as the lead advisor to business process owners in the orchestration and maintenance of a robust internal control environment. This includes championing the integration of risk management principles-including Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance-throughout the end-to-end project lifecycle to ensure risk mitigation is embedded into business operations by design. Control Evaluation and Monitoring: Conduct end-to-end evaluations of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) to ensure the integrity and accuracy of financial disclosures. This responsibility entails executing risk diagnostics, assessing the design and operational effectiveness of controls, mapping key financial statement assertions to control activities, and monitoring the effectiveness of controls. Stakeholder Engagement: Serve as a primary liaison to key stakeholders, including business process owners, as well as internal and external audit teams. Cultivate and maintain professional relationships to facilitate effective communication and alignment on program objectives. Learning and Development: Serve as a subject matter expert in promoting risk awareness across designated business areas. This can be done by facilitating high-level training sessions that translate complex FRM concepts into actionable knowledge, ensuring process owners understand the strategic importance of risk identification and the value of a robust control environment. Deficiency Management and Remediation: Assist in the process for identifying and evaluating control deficiencies. Investigate root causes, partner with business units to ensure corrective action plans are appropriate, and monitor remediation efforts through to successful completion. Process Enhancements and Optimization: Drive continuous improvement initiatives within the organization. Identify and recommend opportunities to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of compliance activities through control optimization, process automation, and the application of data analytics or AI. Team Mentorship and Development: Provide mentorship and professional guidance to new or junior analysts. This includes reviewing work products, delivering constructive feedback, and fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous learning. Reporting and Analysis: Assist in the preparation of clear and concise reports for Financial Risk Management (FRM) leadership and key stakeholders. These communications will articulate the purpose and status of risks related to key initiatives, such as, but not limited to, SOX compliance. This reporting will provide actionable insights that strengthen the organization's risk posture and operational resilience. Regulatory Compliance: Stay abreast of changes in SOX and other related regulations and best practices, and ensure the company's compliance program is updated accordingly. This includes monitoring changes to PCAOB auditing standards and SEC guidance. 

Additional Skills

To be successful in this role, the ideal candidate should possess the following additional skills:

Exceptional Communication: The ability to distill complex financial concepts for any audience, from engineers to executives. You can articulate risk in a way that is clear, concise, and compelling. A Sharp, Analytical Mind: Drive and curiosity to dig into details, connecting the dots between processes, and solving complex puzzles. Solving problems with critical thinking and a meticulous eye for detail. Adaptability and Resilience: A flexible mindset that is comfortable navigating ambiguity and thriving in Uber's fast-paced, ever-evolving environment. Automation & AI Aptitude: A digital-first mindset dedicated to identifying automation opportunities and leveraging emerging AI technologies to scale organizational impact. Digital Transformation Aptitude: Proven ability to identify automation opportunities and leverage emerging AI technologies to enhance risk oversight. The ability to thrive at the nexus of technology and financial risk by championing automated workflows and the deployment of real-time, AI-powered control environments. Strong Business Acumen: A genuine curiosity about how Uber's business operates and the ability to connect the dots between internal controls and our broader strategic goals. Unwavering Integrity: A deep commitment to doing the right thing, with the courage to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct and ethical judgment. 

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. 4+ years of relevant experience in SOX, internal audit, or public accounting (Big 4 experience is a plus). CPA, CA, CIA, CISA, or other relevant professional certification is highly preferred.

rows.descriptionText:
About The Role And Team

As a Staff Scientist at Uber, you will solve the complex, global-scale puzzle of how millions of people and things move in the real world. Operating as a technical multiplier at the high-stakes intersection of digital systems and physical movement, you will navigate extreme ambiguity, set scientific strategy, and make critical decisions with imperfect information. Whether you are architecting next-generation marketplace mechanisms or defining experimentation guardrails, you will thrive in an environment where high performance and massive scale are inextricably linked.

You will join the Rider Pricing and Incentive team, which owns the real-time algorithms powering our mobility business. In this role, you will define the scientific strategy for measuring marketplace performance and optimizing complex pricing systems. Beyond building models, you will develop data insights to identify high-impact opportunities and influence executive roadmaps. You will also drive execution by providing technical guidance to junior scientists and partnering cross-functionally with Product and Engineering teams to deliver high-impact, productionized results.

What You'll Do

 Set Scientific Vision: Define the 1-2 year scientific strategy and technical roadmap for real-time rider pricing, identifying high-impact opportunities.  Lead the Architecture and Design: Define the scientific frameworks and next-generation pricing algorithms that ensure our models are modular, extensible, and observable at global scale.  Act as a Technical Multiplier: Elevate team-wide technical execution by identifying opportunities for system efficiency, model performance, and reduction of technical debt across software and science pipelines.  Influence Senior Leadership: Partner directly with Product, Engineering, and Business Executives, translating complex data and technical findings into clear strategic recommendations.  Own Technical Trajectory: Direct the evolution of critical pricing systems, balancing short-term needs with long-term scalability and efficiency.  Establish Scientific Guardrails: Set experimentation standards and statistical frameworks across multiple teams, driving organization-wide adoption of best practices in causal inference and marketplace testing. 

Basic Qualifications

 Ph.D., M.S., or B.S. in Economics, Operations Research, Statistics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or related quantitative fields.  Minimum of 6+ years (M.S./Ph.D.) or 8+ years (B.S.) of industry experience building, deploying, and scaling quantitative models in production environments.  Deep expertise in statistical inference, advanced experimental design (e.g., switchbacks, cluster-randomized trials), and quantitative economic modeling.  Proficiency in SQL and Python working with large-scale distributed data tools (e.g., Spark, Presto). 

Preferred Qualifications

 Domain Mastery: Recognized expertise in marketplace design, pricing algorithms, industrial organization, ML system design, or large-scale optimization in high-throughput environments.  Technical Vision: Proven track record of anticipating scientific or system bottlenecks 12+ months in advance and building foundational frameworks to address them. About The Role

As a Staff Scientist working on Earner Program Logistics, you will solve high-stakes optimization and marketplace problems at the boundary of digital algorithms and physical-world delivery. Operating as a principal technical multiplier, you will shape the science strategy for core marketplace decisions-ensuring algorithms optimize for long-term platform value and are incentive-compatible.

In this role, you will lead the end-to-end scientific vision for complex logistics systems, partnering with teams across all of Uber to build a balanced, resilient, and highly efficient marketplace for eaters, merchants, and couriers globally.

What You'll Do

 Translate strategically important, unstructured problems into rigorous experiments and productionized solutions that move the needle for the Uber Eats business.  Drive the end-to-end product development lifecycle from a science and data perspective, solving business challenges using Causal Inference and Optimization.  Set the science strategy and experimentation standards across multiple teams, ensuring scientific rigor and driving organization-wide adoption of best practices.  Act as a technical multiplier , identifying opportunities for better performance, efficiency, and reduction of technical debt in models and processes.  Influence executive-level roadmaps by presenting complex technical findings and long-term strategic recommendations to senior leadership.  Own the technical trajectory of critical product areas, ensuring solutions are designed to be extensible, modular, and observable while balancing short-term needs and long-term productivity.

 Ph.D., M.S., or B.S. degree in Operations Research, Economics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or other quantitative fields.  If M.S. degree, a minimum of 6+ years of industry experience required; if B.S. degree, a minimum of 8+ years of industry experience required.  Deep expertise in statistical inference and experimental design (e.g., A/B, switchbacks, cluster-randomized trials).  Proficiency in SQL and Python to work efficiently with large-scale datasets and distributed tools (e.g., Spark, Hive, Presto). 

Preferred Qualifications 

 Technical Vision: A track record of foreseeing architectural or scientific problems 12+ months out and addressing them before they impact the business.  Impact & Scale: Experience leading multi-quarter, cross-functional initiatives that moved significant marketplace or financial metrics in production.  Domain Mastery: Specialized expertise in Causal Inference at scale, Economics, or Marketplace Optimization.

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
In compliance with applicable laws, HSBC is committed to employing only individuals who are authorized to work in the United States. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S., as HSBC will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

Our purpose — Opening up a world of opportunity — explains why we exist. At HSBC, we use our unique expertise, capabilities, breadth and perspectives to open up new kinds of opportunity for our more than 40 million customers. We bring together people, ideas and capital that nurture progress and growth, helping to create a better world — for our customers, our people, our investors, our communities and the planet we all share.

As Senior Audit Manager - Enterprise-wide Risk Management (ERM) and Governance Audit, you will lead audit coverage of ERM and Governance in the US. The ERM and Governance Audit team is responsible for audit coverage of the management of the ERM function and Corporate Governance across HSBC Group, including the management of operational and resilience risks. This is achieved through both direct audit coverage and providing subject-matter expertise to monitor and direct the audit coverage across Global Internal Audit.

As Senior Audit Manager - Enterprise-wide Risk Management (ERM) and Governance Audit, you will:

 Lead a team of 3 audit managers, overseeing delivery of all US audits in the ERM and Governance Audit Plan Interact with local regulators regarding GIA coverage of relevant activities, notably 2LOD oversight of operational and resilience risks Manage the relationship with relevant stakeholders in the US on major plans, projects, strategic developments, and industry trends, both to understand and provide input to emerging risks and issues and assess the impact on the planned schedule of audits. Co-ordinate GIA coverage of applicable regulatory requirements, such as Heightened Standards, across multiple audit teams in the US Effectively manage some individual audits and activity through planning and delivery of the annual audit plan within expected timeframe, standards, methodology, budget, and best practices Confirm that audit findings and recommendations are understood and appropriately addressed Demonstrate knowledge of the applicable business and regulatory environment impacting ERM and Governance, including developing trends, risks, controls, and expectations Support a strong risk and conduct culture across the Group and promote awareness and sound operational and strategic decision-making Critically analyses and determine key drivers of change for area of coverage and assess how these will impact GIA’s engagements Identify audit process improvements to increase productivity and efficiency without impacting effectiveness

Qualifications And Experience

You’ll likely have the following qualifications to succeed in this role:

 Extensive relevant work experience in the Financial Services Sector, with prior experience in internal audit, consultancy, or external audit preferred, but not essential Experience of team management Knowledge of the applicable regulatory requirements in the US and business processes related to ERM and Governance Relevant accounting, audit, analytical, financial, project management, quantitative, risk, and technology skills, qualifications or certifications Undergraduate or graduate degree in business, accounting, mathematics, or social sciences. Preference given to qualified accountants, CIA, CISA, CFE, or ACAMS Fluency in English Willingness to travel Experience in defining and utilizing data-driven techniques including data analytics, process mining & AI is desirable but not essential Analytical and critical thinker, who can effectively manage competing priorities and complex challenges to deliver positive outcomes and apply technology or expertise to business issues or operational problems

We're looking for a storyteller, communications specialist, or a producer to build and scale Uber's technical thought leadership platform.

Reporting to the Head of Product Communications, you'll own how Uber's technology story comes to life across podcast, executive social, and earned media. You'll lead the editorial strategy and production of a monthly podcast hosted by Uber's CTO, while partnering with engineering leaders to elevate the people and technologies shaping the future of mobility and delivery, AI, and marketplace innovation.

This role is equal parts editorial director, executive producer, and communications strategist. You'll identify the stories worth telling, shape compelling narratives, secure high-impact guests, produce compelling and differentiated content, and amplify those stories across social, press, and owned channels to strengthen Uber's position as a destination for top technical talent and innovators.

This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about engineering, thrives in ambiguity, loves building new editorial products from the ground up, and has the creativity, judgment, and execution skills to produce work that stands out in a crowded technology landscape.

 Own the end-to-end editorial vision, production, and execution of Uber's new external technology podcast-from concept development through recording, editing, publishing, promotion, and performance analysis.  Partner directly with Uber's CTO and senior engineering leaders to develop authentic, insightful conversations that elevate Uber's technical leadership.  Develop and execute thoughtful executive social media strategies-primarily on X-to amplify the voices of Uber's technology leaders and extend the reach of key technical narratives. Spot emerging technology trends and develop timely editorial that resonates with technical audiences around AI, machine learning, infrastructure, autonomy, cybersecurity, and the future of software engineering.  Apply strong editorial judgment to translate complex technical work into simple, compelling stories without sacrificing technical credibility. Established relationships with technology reporters, influential creators, researchers, founders, and AI industry leaders. rows.title: Senior Manager, Launch Excellence

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

At Uber, great products are only as good as the experiences they create - and customer experience doesn't begin when a ticket arrives. It begins the moment a new feature or product launch decision is made.

Ensuring that customer experience is at the forefront of the design and build of every new product feature, enhancement, or net new launch means we must influence product design upstream - before painful experiences occur or support issues arrive at our doorstep.

This is the foundational belief behind this role. The Senior Manager, CX Launch Excellence - Mobility, will be the single point of contact responsible for defining the governance model and best practices to enable the right PoCs from CommOps to be embedded as a strategic partner across the Product Development Lifecycle. From PRD through go-to-market to hypercare, this person ensures that a consistent process is followed for every product, feature, and operational change so that the change and/or rollout ships with a customer experience that is excellent from day one - at every maturity level.

This is not a reactive support role. The primary accountability for this role is launch governance and CX readiness standards - defining the frameworks, gates, and operating model that determine how customer experience teams engage in the product development process.

What You'll Own

 Build the Definitive Playbook for CX Participation in the Product Development Lifecycle: Define and own the end-to-end standard for how Community Operations engages across every stage of product development - from PRD through product development checkpoint reviews to launch and hypercare for Mobility. 

Design a tiered engagement model that distinguishes the right level of CX involvement based on product portfolio type: core product lines, growth initiatives, or emerging bets. Every product that ships a customer experience must meet the bar - and this role sets that bar.

Build and maintain the master playbook covering intake criteria, readiness gates, go/no-go frameworks, escalation triggers, and accountability structures. So there is never ambiguity about where CX stands in the process. Establish clear principles: CX is not a reviewer at the end of the pipeline but a co-designer from the beginning.

 Own and Govern the Intake Process - The "Front Door" for Cross functional partners : Design and operate the intake and triage system that captures all customer-impacting changes across Mobility - product launches, feature iterations, quality testing, platform rollouts. Define the criteria and guardrails that determine which changes require full CX readiness reviews, which require lightweight checkpoints, and who is accountable for driving each gate. Create the organizational mechanisms - forums, decision rights, SLAs, tooling - that ensure every change traverses a standard readiness process with full visibility, no matter how fast the business moves. This person is the single point of accountability for XFN partners (including Product) knowing exactly when to loop in CX and what to expect when they do.  Embed CX as a Strategic Partner in Every Launch: Act as the primary counterpart for Mobility Customer Experience, Product Insights & Rollout, Product Ops, and Customer Obsession teams as they seek to not only review launches, but to shape them. Establish clear engagement rules, decision paths, and escalation protocols so upstream teams know exactly how and when to plug in CX - making the partnership predictable, high-trust, and efficient. Build relationships with product/product ops teams to drive this forward.  Define and Drive Support Readiness Standards Across the Portfolio: Translate every upstream product, ops, and policy change into concrete CX readiness requirements: content, macros, workflows, training, tooling, escalation paths - with clear owners and delivery timelines. Track and ensure CX feedback has been formally acknowledged and resolved before launch gates are cleared. Hold go/no-go authority at defined readiness gates with clear escalation paths to senior leadership when standards are not met, ensuring CX readiness is never treated as optional, including structured pre-launch testing protocols that validate support readiness before go-live.  Partner with Analytics and S&P: Work with the Analytics and Insights team to build dashboards and alerting that make launch health and readiness gaps visible to leadership - and actionable before they become incidents. Advocate for customer experience metrics to be embedded in product launch success criteria from the outset. Use data, agent feedback, and customer signals to systematically identify structural upstream causes of defects - and drive resolution through product and policy, not just support responses.  Lead Through Influence and Build Organizational Capability: Operate as a senior leader who drives clarity, builds structure, and governance standards across Product, CX, Product Insights & Rollout/Product ops - primarily without direct authority. Build and govern a networked model of CX readiness owners across personas; set the standards and ways of working while enabling execution. Scale "launch excellence" as an organizational capability - not just a team function - by embedding frameworks, tools, and habits across Community Operations. 

Why This Role Matters

Every product in Uber's Mobility portfolio ships a customer experience. And right now, CX is too often looped in too late - after the design is locked, the product development checkpoint reviews process is well underway, and the support readiness is not embedded into the design. This role changes that permanently.

The person who fills this seat will build the infrastructure - the playbook, the intake process, the governance model, the standards - that ensures CX is never an afterthought. They will be the reason Mobility launches are smoother, right CX inputs are shared during design and build so features are desgined to be defect free, and customers feel the quality of what we build from day one.

Basic Qualifications

 Minimum 6 years of experience in technical program management, product ops, product management, strategy & operations, or similar roles  Bachelors Degree 

Preferred Qualifications

 10+ years of experience in technical program management, product operations, or strategy & operations, specifically within customer support or service operations supporting platforms with >10M active users.  Track record of building and deploying at least 2 end-to-end launch governance frameworks or operational playbooks from 0-to-1 (initial build through full operational rollout).  Prior experience at a consumer technology, mobility, marketplace, travel, or e-commerce company with >$500M in annual revenue or equivalent operational scale.  Governance, Launch Gates & Cross-Functional Operations  Demonstrated management of go/no-go launch gate decisions across 10+ major product feature rollouts.  Experience engaging upstream during the Product Requirement Document (PRD) or initial design phase for at least 50% of managed product launches.  Proven track record of leading cross-functional alignment across 5+ distinct stakeholder departments (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Operations, and Product Ops) without direct report authority.  Experience authoring metric frameworks and partnering with analytics teams to build executive-facing dashboards (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, SQL-based tools) for tracking launch health KPIs.  Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience configuring, deploying, or managing content governance for AI-powered support tooling (e.g., LLM virtual assistants, intelligent routing, or agent-assist systems).  Experience reviewing technical design documents, system flowcharts, and architecture specs with Engineering and ML/AI teams to extract support readiness requirements.  Experience writing executive-level decision memos, QBRs, or go/no-go scorecards presented directly to VP-level leadership

rows.title: Senior - FRM Advisory
rows.descriptionText:
About Team

At Uber, we're not just moving people and things; we're building a global business grounded in integrity. Our Financial Risk Management (FRM) Advisory team is the backbone of that integrity, ensuring our financial reporting is accurate, trustworthy, and compliant with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX).

As a Senior on this team, you'll be on the front lines, safeguarding our financial data and helping us navigate the complexities of a dynamic, global company. This isn't just about checking boxes-it's about asking the right questions, acting with conviction, and boldly improving our processes to drive meaningful outcomes and maintain the trust of our stakeholders.

What You Will Do

Uber's technology platform reimagines the way people and things move in cities around the world by connecting drivers, riders, and eaters. We offer a variety of services including:

Ridesharing: Connecting riders with drivers for convenient transportation. Delivery: Connecting consumers with restaurants and stores for food, groceries, and other deliveries. Freight: Connecting shippers and carriers in the logistics space. 

Job Responsibilities - FRM Advisory Senior - Business Process

Strategic Risk Advisory & Governance: Serve as the lead advisor to business process owners in the orchestration and maintenance of a robust internal control environment. This includes championing the integration of risk management principles-including Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance-throughout the end-to-end project lifecycle to ensure risk mitigation is embedded into business operations by design. Control Evaluation and Monitoring: Conduct end-to-end evaluations of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) to ensure the integrity and accuracy of financial disclosures. This responsibility entails executing risk diagnostics, assessing the design and operational effectiveness of controls, mapping key financial statement assertions to control activities, and monitoring the effectiveness of controls. Stakeholder Engagement: Serve as a primary liaison to key stakeholders, including business process owners, as well as internal and external audit teams. Cultivate and maintain professional relationships to facilitate effective communication and alignment on program objectives. Learning and Development: Serve as a subject matter expert in promoting risk awareness across designated business areas. This can be done by facilitating high-level training sessions that translate complex FRM concepts into actionable knowledge, ensuring process owners understand the strategic importance of risk identification and the value of a robust control environment. Deficiency Management and Remediation: Assist in the process for identifying and evaluating control deficiencies. Investigate root causes, partner with business units to ensure corrective action plans are appropriate, and monitor remediation efforts through to successful completion. Process Enhancements and Optimization: Drive continuous improvement initiatives within the organization. Identify and recommend opportunities to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of compliance activities through control optimization, process automation, and the application of data analytics or AI. Team Mentorship and Development: Provide mentorship and professional guidance to new or junior analysts. This includes reviewing work products, delivering constructive feedback, and fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous learning. Reporting and Analysis: Assist in the preparation of clear and concise reports for Financial Risk Management (FRM) leadership and key stakeholders. These communications will articulate the purpose and status of risks related to key initiatives, such as, but not limited to, SOX compliance. This reporting will provide actionable insights that strengthen the organization's risk posture and operational resilience. Regulatory Compliance: Stay abreast of changes in SOX and other related regulations and best practices, and ensure the company's compliance program is updated accordingly. This includes monitoring changes to PCAOB auditing standards and SEC guidance. 

Additional Skills

To be successful in this role, the ideal candidate should possess the following additional skills:

Exceptional Communication: The ability to distill complex financial concepts for any audience, from engineers to executives. You can articulate risk in a way that is clear, concise, and compelling. A Sharp, Analytical Mind: Drive and curiosity to dig into details, connecting the dots between processes, and solving complex puzzles. Solving problems with critical thinking and a meticulous eye for detail. Adaptability and Resilience: A flexible mindset that is comfortable navigating ambiguity and thriving in Uber's fast-paced, ever-evolving environment. Automation & AI Aptitude: A digital-first mindset dedicated to identifying automation opportunities and leveraging emerging AI technologies to scale organizational impact. Digital Transformation Aptitude: Proven ability to identify automation opportunities and leverage emerging AI technologies to enhance risk oversight. The ability to thrive at the nexus of technology and financial risk by championing automated workflows and the deployment of real-time, AI-powered control environments. Strong Business Acumen: A genuine curiosity about how Uber's business operates and the ability to connect the dots between internal controls and our broader strategic goals. Unwavering Integrity: A deep commitment to doing the right thing, with the courage to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct and ethical judgment. 

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. 4+ years of relevant experience in SOX, internal audit, or public accounting (Big 4 experience is a plus). CPA, CA, CIA, CISA, or other relevant professional certification is highly preferred.

Science and Engineering at Uber mean building for real-world impact under real-world constraints. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will work at the high-stakes intersection of economics, statistics, and computer science to build the intelligent systems that power our global marketplaces. Unlike purely analytics roles, this is a production-focused position where you will turn "messy" behavioral data into scalable, machine-readable insights and automated decision-making engines.

You will join a high-stakes environment where the work is fast-moving, and the systems you build directly affect how millions of people and things move across our global platforms every single day. Collaborating closely with Product and Engineering, you will lead high-visibility projects from conceptualization to global productionization, navigating technical debt and shifting priorities along the way. If you are a systems-thinker who stays calm under pressure and is motivated to build production-grade models that solve unstructured problems without a textbook solution, this is where you'll grow.

What You'll Do

 Build and deploy production-grade ML models and statistical algorithms that enhance platform intelligence and user experience in real-time environments.  Design complex experiments and causal inference frameworks to interpret results and drive trade-offs between short-term wins and long-term system reliability. Advanced coding proficiency with the ability to contribute to production-level codebases and develop modular tools re-used across teams. About The Role

Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. This team is focused on the hardest problem in AV today: unlocking real-world, long-tail driving data. Autonomy is now a data race-and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.

You will be at the forefront of Physical AI, building advanced autonomy algorithms to add rich semantics to our massive driving data. You will be responsible for the development and implementation of the latest autonomy techniques that enables better data mining, deep scene understanding, and causal modeling of ego vehicle behavior.The ideal candidate will be able to identify complex edge cases, provide robust algorithmic solutions, and set a high technical excellence bar.

 Algorithm Development: Develop algorithms that extract high-fidelity semantic meaning from complex urban edge cases to enrich our L4 data lake. rows.descriptionText:
About The Role And Team

Uber's Commercial Sales Enablement team supports our multi-billion dollar Delivery business, including Uber Eats, Grocery & Retail, and Direct lines of business. We equip our sales teams with the capabilities, tools, insights, and processes needed to increase seller and account manager productivity, accelerate growth, and improve merchant outcomes. As the US&C Enablement Lead, you will own the enablement strategy and execution for one of Uber's largest and most dynamic commercial regions, serving as a strategic partner to Sales, Operations, Product, and global Enablement leaders.

In this role, you will translate global priorities and major product, policy, and technology changes into locally relevant programs while identifying and addressing the unique capability and performance needs of US&C sellers and managers. From accelerating new-hire productivity and strengthening sales and manager capabilities to enabling critical GTM launches and driving adoption of seller technology and AI, you will lead a portfolio of work designed to change seller behavior and improve commercial performance.

This role requires someone who can move seamlessly between strategy and execution, influence senior stakeholders, use data to prioritize where Enablement can have the greatest impact, and lead a team that helps US&C commercial teams perform at their best.

What You'll Do

 Lead the US&C Revenue Enablement strategy and roadmap, translating commercial priorities, performance data, seller needs, and global initiatives into a focused portfolio of programs that improve seller productivity, capability, and business outcomes.  Partner with senior leaders across Sales, Operations, Product, Marketing, Sales Operations, and Global Enablement to diagnose performance opportunities, establish priorities, define success measures, and align stakeholders on enablement plans and trade-offs.  Drive readiness and adoption for complex product, policy, process, seller technology, and AI transformations, using Uber's GTM intake and tiering processes to coordinate stakeholder alignment, communications, training, manager reinforcement, launch execution, and post-launch adoption.  Build scalable capability programs across the seller lifecycle-including Fast Start onboarding, sales academies, negotiation and solution-selling programs, and frontline manager development-connecting learning to observable seller behaviors and commercial performance.  Leverage platforms and data including Seismic, Salesforce, Tableau, conversational intelligence, and emerging AI tools to personalize enablement, improve content discovery, identify performance gaps, measure adoption, and increase seller and manager productivity.  Measure enablement effectiveness with a disciplined measurement framework spanning learner readiness, behavior and tool adoption, seller productivity, and business outcomes; maintain accurate reporting and communicate progress, risks, insights, and recommendations to senior stakeholders.  Lead and develop the US&C Enablement team, setting clear priorities and operating rhythms, allocating capacity across strategic initiatives, GTM launches, and emerging regional needs, and maintaining a high bar for execution quality, stakeholder partnership, and measurable impact.  Influence the broader commercial organization through clear, concise executive communication, translating complex initiatives and performance signals into actionable recommendations while proactively surfacing dependencies, competing priorities, and risks to successful execution. 

Basic qualifications 

 A minimum of 8 years of professional experience in Revenue/Sales Enablement, Sales Excellence, Learning & Development, Commercial Operations, Sales Operations, or a related field, including experience supporting a complex sales or go-to-market organization.  A minimum of 3 years of experience leading teams, major programs, or cross-functional workstreams with accountability for strategy, prioritization, stakeholder alignment, and execution.  Demonstrated experience partnering with senior Sales, Operations, Product, Marketing, and/or Sales Operations leaders to translate business priorities and performance gaps into scalable enablement solutions.  Experience leading complex go-to-market or organizational change initiatives, including product, process, policy, sales methodology, technology, or AI/tool adoption, with responsibility for communications, readiness, execution, reinforcement, and measurement.  Experience using sales and enablement technology such as Salesforce and Seismic, or comparable CRM, LMS/content management, analytics, and seller productivity platforms, to manage programs, drive adoption, and evaluate impact.  Demonstrated ability to use quantitative and qualitative data to identify performance gaps, prioritize investments, maintain accurate reporting, and measure outcomes such as seller productivity, ramp time, adoption, conversion, or revenue performance.  Demonstrated experience applying AI and automation to design, deliver, and scale enablement programs, including using AI-powered tools to improve learning, content, workflows, personalization, or seller productivity.  Professional working proficiency in English, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex strategies, performance insights, risks, and recommendations clearly and accurately to both executive and frontline audiences.  Must be able to work from the designated US&C Uber office/hub according to Uber's applicable hybrid work schedule and travel within the US&C region as required to support commercial leaders, teams, and key enablement programs.  Willingness to travel within US&C as needed (up to 20%). 

Preferred qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree in Business, Organizational Development, Learning & Development, Communications, or a related field preferred; MBA or other relevant advanced degree is a plus.  Strong proficiency with data and analytics, including the ability to interpret commercial performance data, diagnose productivity and capability gaps, establish success metrics, and translate insights into clear recommendations for senior leaders.  Experience supporting enterprise or complex B2B sales organizations, with a strong understanding of sales motions, pipeline management, account management, solution selling, negotiation, and frontline sales management.  Experience designing and executing large-scale change management and GTM programs across multiple teams, functions, business lines, or geographies. About The Role

Our mission is to protect, defend, and secure Uber's products, infrastructure, and data by building highly available, scalable, and extensible security solutions and services. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with IT, product, and various security teams to strengthen response readiness and posture across the entire environment. Proficiency in programming languages such as Golang, Java, or Python.  Deep understanding of distributed systems, high-availability, and high-performance system design.  Hands-on experience with Cyber Defense such as incident response, threat hunting, and investigation.  Master's Degree or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security or a related field.  Prior experience leading incident response, threat hunting, digital forensics, and building AI-driven response tooling.  Deep experience incorporating GenAI agents into production security services, specifically for investigation, triage, or automated response. rows.title: Senior Product Manager - Search, Discovery & Open Innovation
rows.descriptionText:
Dr. Martens is more than a brand - it’s a global icon with over 60 years of attitude, heritage, and cultural impact. We’re a thriving, values‑driven business powered by diverse thinkers, bold doers, and people who bring their whole selves to work. If you’re ready to make your mark, you’re in the right place.

At DM, our values guide everything we do: Be Yourself, Act Courageously, Show You Care. They’re not just words - they’re how we turn passion into progress.

WHERE YOU SIT

As our Senior Product Manager – Search, Discovery & Open Innovation, you’ll be part of the Consumer & Brand team working closely with brilliant people across the business and reporting into Head of Global Customer Product. You’ll be right at the heart of fast‑moving projects that shape how we show up for our consumers - today and tomorrow.

WHERE YOU CONTRIBUTE

This role is not a delivery role but a design leadership and craft role.

The Senior Product Manager owns the Search & Discovery experience as a product across channels, defining how customers find, explore, and engage with Dr. Martens across digital and physical touchpoints. This includes not only search, navigation, and discovery online, but also how discovery is supported through retail, campaigns, content, and emerging interfaces.

This role also leads open innovation for the entire product team, identifying and scaling new technologies, partnerships, and capabilities that enhance discovery and create competitive differentiation as we move towards a more premium positioning.

Sitting at the intersection of product, experience design, technology, data, brand, and commercial, this role ensures discovery is seamless, intuitive, and elevated across the full customer journey.

Core Accountabilities

As our Senior Product Manager – Search, Discovery & Open Innovation, you will be responsible for:

Owning the global Search & Discovery experience, defining the product strategy, customer value proposition and roadmap across digital and physical touchpoints to make product discovery intuitive, inspiring and relevant. Setting the vision and principles for discovery, translating customer needs, market context and data into focused priorities while ensuring consistent, differentiated and premium experiences across channels. Driving continuous product improvement, optimising search relevance, navigation, merchandising logic and discovery journeys through experimentation, testing and iteration to reduce friction and improve commercial outcomes. Leading innovation and emerging technology, exploring and scaling new capabilities including AI-powered search, recommendations, conversational interfaces and innovations from start-up ecosystems. Building a connected, insight-led discovery ecosystem, partnering with Experience Design, Technology, Data, Retail, Commercial and markets to create strong feedback loops and ensure customer behaviour continuously informs product decisions, while role-modelling the practical use of AI in product thinking and leadership. 


Key Skills & Capabilities

Put simply, the key things we’re looking for are:

Strong Search & Discovery expertise, with deep knowledge of search, navigation, taxonomy, filtering, recommendations and digital commerce discovery experiences. Strong product strategy and prioritisation capability, able to define and communicate a clear vision and roadmap based on customer needs, data, experimentation and commercial outcomes. A data-driven and innovative mindset, confident using analytics and customer behaviour to identify opportunities, test new ideas and balance BAU delivery with emerging innovation. Strong AI and emerging technology capability, with experience applying AI to areas such as search, personalisation, recommendations or insight generation, and a responsible, practical approach to using AI in product development. Exceptional cross-functional influence and communication, able to work with senior Technology, Experience, Data and Market stakeholders globally, simplify complex concepts and drive alignment and decisions.

Hybrid workingWelcome free pair of Docs‘Buy as you Earn’ Share scheme 65% off all Docs50% off AccessoriesPension Scheme through AvivaLife Assurance 25 Days Annual Leave + Bank Holidays Private healthcare2 paid volunteer days per year


READY TO FILL YOUR BOOTS?

This role leads the Acquisition Growth & Optimisation team — the intelligence, audience and experimentation engine at the top of the customer funnel. The role partners with the Senior Manager, Retention Growth & Optimisation to ensure a consistent, insight-led approach across the full customer lifecycle.

The role drives new customer acquisition by identifying, sizing and prioritising opportunities across the upper funnel and first-purchase journey, and by improving Cost to Acquire; optimising across audience quality, channel mix, media efficiency and conversion into first purchase.

The role is accountable for the quality of acquisition, not simply its volume. The priority is to rebuild a stronger acquisition engine that recruits customers worth keeping (predicted 12M CLTV). In practice the role answers three questions for the business: who to target, where to invest, and how to continuously improve acquisition efficiency and quality.

The role embeds test-and-learn, audience and suppression governance, and incrementality-based measurement into acquisition activity, ensuring media investment and customer journeys are continuously improved and deliver measurable, efficient and profitable growth.

Core Accountabilities

As our Senior Manager Acquisition Growth & Optimisation you will be responsible for:

Identifying and prioritising acquisition opportunities across channels, audiences and markets, sizing and sequencing opportunities based on value, feasibility and impact.Defining and owning the global audience strategy, developing segmentation frameworks and ensuring consistent, insight-led targeting and activation across channels, markets and campaigns.Driving acquisition quality and effectiveness, using LTV:CAC, New vs Repeat and marginal ROAS to optimise investment towards sustainable, high-value customer growth.Leading optimisation, experimentation and performance insight, overseeing the global testing roadmap, identifying opportunities to improve CAC, conversion and LTV, and translating data into clear commercial recommendations.Enabling markets and aligning cross-functional teams, providing audience frameworks and playbooks while partnering with Customer Growth, Commercial, CRM, Data & Analytics, Product, eCommerce and Experience teams to connect global strategy with local execution.
